### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via boundary_event (literal, a string literal in scanUnreachableNodes))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ebc2cdc52207e0e755a910afeda65a39630a84fa` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bbb1341eddff0b0fcf4cd3ee59abd22da8ecf813` — the merge of head `0a1def67c464136ffbf5eca8a88dfd9f3012be8d` into base `ebc2cdc52207e0e755a910afeda65a39630a84fa`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bbb1341eddff0b0fcf4cd3ee59abd22da8ecf813 && git checkout bbb1341eddff0b0fcf4cd3ee59abd22da8ecf813
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ebc2cdc52207e0e755a910afeda65a39630a84fa 0a1def67c464136ffbf5eca8a88dfd9f3012be8d && git checkout -B drift-repro ebc2cdc52207e0e755a910afeda65a39630a84fa && git merge --no-ff 0a1def67c464136ffbf5eca8a88dfd9f3012be8d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ebc2cdc52207e0e755a910afeda65a39630a84fa
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ebc2cdc52207e0e755a910afeda65a39630a84fa` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d3db24b18b145d587eea50ec97ad696a96ba33fa`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/31224-flow-node-unreachable.md, packages/lint/src/index.ts, packages/lint/src/lint-flow-patterns.ts, packages/lint/src/lint-flow-patterns.test.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.draft-publish-verdict.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.metadata-redaction.test.ts + packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/control-flow.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-create-seeds.ts, packages/spec/src/conversions/entries/17/retry-policy-converged.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/dag-traversal.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-registration-checks.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-flow-trigger-readiness.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-history-and-publish.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/metadata-diagnostics.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/automation/flows/index.ts, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, hotcrm src/revenue/flows/quote-expiration.flow.ts, src/sales/flows/forecast-snapshot.flow.ts, src/marketing/flows/campaign-completion.flow.ts

Inputs read: card #31224 body and every comment (triage 6711648543, claim 6712039823, plan 6712129038, seat rulings 6712144718, os-dev-report 6713825906); PR #31287 body, file list and `git diff origin/main...d3db24b1` (merge-base `8f4e8fb9`, 7 files, +305/-10); the check-runs on `d3db24b1` and the failed job's log; for the Clause-② precedent, PR #30003 (the PR that fixed card #29900 — #29900 itself is the issue, not a PR) with its changeset `46d2b6503`. Judged on the committed tree, not the PR body's account of it; the dev's census numbers were not re-run (read-only), the corpus statements below are greps against `objectstack` at `d3db24b1` and `hotcrm` at `6961ab1`. This record is served at the tier `reviewFace` owes for a `(narrowing)` arm on the declaration texts (the narrowing face, `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`), replacing the earlier declaration-face reading of the same head.

### ① Derived judgments

**The rule, against the engine it describes — right.** `scanUnreachableNodes` (`packages/lint/src/lint-flow-patterns.ts`) picks `nodes.find(type === 'start')`, exactly the engine's own choice (`service-automation/src/dag-traversal.ts:1240`, `engine.ts:6217`: first `start` in array order, else `FLOW_NO_START_NODE`), then walks every top-level edge by `source`. `traverseNext` (`dag-traversal.ts:562`) schedules a top-level node only by out-edge: conditional and default edges when selected, `back` edges like any other, `fault` edges on the failure path. Nothing else schedules a top-level node (no `nextNodeId`/`targetNodeId` reference exists in `builtin-node-config.zod.ts`). So "every edge type is a path" is the engine's truth and the BFS with a `reached` set is correct on cycles (pinned: a cycle cut off from start gives one finding per node).

**Start-node cases — right, one wording nit.** No `start` ⇒ not judged (the engine refuses the run anyway). Two `start` nodes: the spec has no one-start rule, the engine and every reader (`flow-registration-checks.ts:371`, `validate-flow-trigger-readiness.ts:563`) use the first, so a second `start` is genuinely never run and is now refused — a correct narrowing. Should-fix (wording, not blocking): on a node of type `start` the hint "Add an edge into it from a node that runs" prescribes the wrong cure (the fix is to remove the extra start); a type-conditional hint or a sentence in the `os explain` entry would close it.

**Edges to or from missing nodes — right.** The scan returns without judging when any edge endpoint is not a node id. That branch is reached only by a document the flow parse has already refused: `lintFlowPatterns` is registered `input: 'parsed'` (`authoring-rules.ts:1964-1974`), so at `os lint/validate/build` the dangling-edge refusal (`flow.zod.ts:1809-1870`) lands first, and at the save door the `FlowSchema.safeParse` at `protocol-save.ts:1429` precedes `assertRuntimeAuthoringRules` at `:1677`. No wrong-cure double report.

**ADR-0031 regions — right.** Containers carry their body as a nested graph in `config.body` / `config.branches[]` / `config.try` / `config.catch` (`control-flow.zod.ts:15-40`, adoption (B)); inner nodes never appear in the top-level `nodes[]`, and the call site hands the scan the top-level lists only, before the (b)–(e) per-region scans. A legacy flat `loop` with no `config.body` keeps its body at top level, reached by edges from the loop node — judged, correctly. A `subflow` node is an ordinary node. Fault/error edges count as paths (control pinned).

**`boundary_event` exemption — lenient, declared, acceptable.** The platform registers no executor for `boundary_event` (`flow.zod.ts:457-460`, `NO_EXECUTOR` plus a startup warn; zero references in `service-automation/src`), so a node reached only from one also never runs today. The PR exempts both and says why; that is under-refusal, never a false refusal, and the boundary contract is the right owner. Not a finding.

**Which doors refuse, which keep.** The rule sits in a `gating` rule with `surfaces: CLI_AND_RUNTIME`, `commands: ALL`, `runtimeTypes: ['flow']`, so: `os lint`, `os validate`, `os build` fail; the live (active) save `PUT /api/v1/meta/flow/NAME` is refused 422 (`protocol-save.ts:1677`); draft→active publish and the package-draft publish batch are refused (`protocol-history-and-publish.ts:950`, same judge, `pending` batch); **and the history restore door** (`protocol-authoring-gate.ts:162`, judged as `active`) — a stored flow version holding an unreached node can no longer be restored. The PR body does not name the restore door; the behaviour is consistent and correct, named here so the seat knows the full set. Drafts are kept: `judgeRuntimeAuthoringRules` returns clean for `state !== 'active'` (`protocol-authoring-gate.ts:317`, #26188 D1 "no rule gates a draft") and the read folds the publish verdict into `_diagnostics` (`metadata-diagnostics.ts:416-441`, `valid: false`). The `package-author` channel returns clean (`:316`), `migrate-stored` returns clean, and `defineStack` at boot runs no lint — so an artifact-backed stack is caught at `os build`, not at boot or install. The `edgesAfterNodeRemoval` designer shape saves as a draft and is refused only on publish or active save — the declared behaviour, and the right one for a node that never runs.

**Shipped and example flows — none refused.** Every `edges: []` in shipped source is a region body or an edgeless single-node flow: `examples/app-showcase/src/automation/flows/index.ts:989,1007` (try region and loop body), `packages/spec/src/conversions/entries/17/retry-policy-converged.ts` (try regions; `roll_up` has only a start), `packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-create-seeds.ts:73-74` (the flow create seed is `nodes: []`, so no start ⇒ not judged — the create door keeps working); hotcrm `6961ab1`: `quote-expiration.flow.ts:48`, `forecast-snapshot.flow.ts:225`, `campaign-completion.flow.ts:56`, all region bodies. `Dogfood Regression Gate` concluded success on this head, which builds the example apps. `packages/spec` is byte-identical to `origin/main` (`git diff --stat` empty), as claimed.

**Tests — behaviour right, one type error (must-fix, ③).** The six re-wired lint fixtures and the approval case each keep their own assertion (compared against `origin/main`); the `relocate` redaction fixture turns `begin` into an assignment, so `e2` is the correct wiring and the two edge-id pins follow. The new describe pins the three refusals, the five controls and the registration; the `CASES` row in `protocol.draft-publish-verdict.test.ts` makes "draft saves `valid:false`, publish refuses, package publish rolls back" a CI fact rather than a body claim. The redaction test's module-top `import '@objectstack/lint'` is the `check:test-source-alias` remedy, not a behaviour change. The registration case in `lint-flow-patterns.test.ts` does not compile under the package's `tsconfig.test.json` — see ③.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset `@objectstack/lint: minor` — right.** AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3: a `Metadata-protocol` kind other than `none` takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves; `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` level axis: `narrowed` must grade at least one moved package `minor` and must sit beside a `(narrowing)` arm — both hold; `Check Changeset` concluded success on this head. BREAKING banner present; ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` present with its reason (no key moves; a never-run node has no meaning-preserving rewrite), the same disposition as `46d2b6503`.
- **`Metadata-protocol: narrowed` — right.** A flow an author could write is now refused: "a value refused or a requirement tightened is `narrowed`" (step 3).
- **`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` — right; the claim's `no (narrowing)` is superseded.** The value answers one question, 「本卡放宽接受集或扩大公开面吗」 (`scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, the fleet's one reader): adding `FLOW_NODE_UNREACHABLE` to the `@objectstack/lint` entry (`index.ts`) and a `RULE_EXPLANATIONS` key widens the public surface ⇒ `yes`; the refusal ⇒ `(narrowing)`; the reader defines `yes (narrowing)` as exactly "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another — both facts are true and both are read". The claim's `no (narrowing)` (6712039823 as amended in 6712144718) was written for the plan's parse-level rule with "no new export" (6712129038 §C); once the rule moved to lint and exported its id, `no` would be false. Precedent `46d2b6503` (PR #30003, fixing card #29900) declared `yes (narrowing)` for the same reason and recorded the same claim-to-PR deviation in its acceptance notes. Body and changeset agree; no edit needed. Either arm carries `(narrowing)`, so the review face and this record's tier are the same under both.
- **The `!` in `fix(lint)!:` — no mechanical effect, not misleading.** No script or workflow reads a title `!` (none in `scripts/`, `scripts/pm/`, `.github/workflows/`; no commitlint). It survives into the squash title as the conventional-commits breaking marker, consistent with the BREAKING banner and with `46d2b6503`; the level is compiled from `.changeset/`, never from the title. The one reader is `.claude/agents/os-dev.md:273`, which makes the dev run the full dogfood battery — done (6713825906 `dogfood_battery`).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **MUST-FIX — the required `TypeScript Type Check` context is red on this head, and the cause is this PR's own edit.** `Type Check · workspace` concluded failure: `@objectstack/lint#typecheck` exits 1 in its `check:test-typecheck` step, "`src/lint-flow-patterns.test.ts`: 1 type error(s) in a file the ledger does not cover. Fix them — this file is inside the checked zone"; the ledger (`test-typecheck-debt.json`) is shrink-only and may not be expanded to clear it (its own text; AGENTS.md Build & Test). The aggregate `TypeScript Type Check` (one of the eleven required contexts, Multi-agent discipline §7) therefore concluded failure. Read, not compiled: the one line in the diff that does not fit its type is the new registration case's `rule!.run(reachFlow(…) as never)` — `AuthoringRule.run` is `(stack: AnyRec, ctx: AuthoringRuleContext)` (`authoring-rules.ts`, the interface at `:444`), and every other call site in the package passes a context (`lint-flow-patterns.test.ts:3207-3208`, `non-record-object-entry.test.ts:109,165`, `runtime-gate.inert-type-writes.test.ts:802`, all `rule.run(stack, {})`); vitest ignores the missing argument at run time, which is why the dev's 254/254 held while `tsc` under `tsconfig.test.json` did not. Fix: pass `{}` as the second argument (or type the stack and call through `lintFlowPatterns` directly); then the whole `TypeScript Type Check` job re-runs on the new head. The dev's gate report (6713825906) lists 62 derived gates exit 0 on `8f731d6a`, which this red contradicts for the lint typecheck — data point for the seat, not re-judged here.
- **Dev `open_questions[0]` (Clause-② arm): answered — `yes (narrowing)` stands** (② above). No body edit, no push.
- **Should-fix (PR body, no push): the `Skills-docs:` line is missing from the PR body.** The pm-dispatch template (`.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md`, `Metadata-protocol` row) says a `(narrowing)` arm owes the PR body a third line-initial declaration; the changeset carries `Skills-docs: none — …` (and its reason checks out: `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`'s edgeless examples are region bodies), the body does not. No CI gate reads it (grep of `scripts/` finds only a comment), so it is seat protocol, not a red — copy the changeset's line into the body.
- **Should-fix (wording): the hint on a refused second `start` node** (① above).
- **Tier of this record:** served at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on the narrowing face, the tier `reviewFace` (`scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs`) owes for a `(narrowing)` arm on any declaration text, `yes (narrowing)` included.
- **Dev flags carried, none blocking:** the runtime suite ran on a pre-merge tree, not the final head (dogfood on `8f731d6a` and CI `Test Core` on `d3db24b1` cover it; the one red named touches no flow); the restore door is an additional refusal site not named in the body (① above, correct behaviour).
- **Check-runs on `d3db24b1` at this read:** failure — `Type Check · workspace` and `TypeScript Type Check` (required; the must-fix above), and `Test Core (8/8)` (required): two packages each lost one test to "Test timed out in 5000ms" on a loaded runner — `examples/app-todo` `test/loop-body-iteration.test.ts:134` (a run of `OverdueEscalationFlow`, whose top-level graph is fully wired `start → get_overdue_tasks → loop_overdue → end`, so this rule did not refuse it: a refusal would be a 422, not a timeout; the log shows connection-acquire aborts around it) and `packages/qa/scenarios` `test/runner/external-driver.test.ts:176` (a full crm run through the external driver) — neither file is in this diff and neither reads a flow this diff changes, so they are not attributed to the PR; they clear only with the fix push, which re-runs the shard (Multi-agent discipline §7: never by re-running alone). Success — `Lint & Repo Gates` (required) and every `Lint ·` lane, `Build Core` (required), `Dogfood Regression Gate` (required), `Governed Surface Queue Guard` (required), `Build & E2E UI` (required), `Live E2E UI` (required), `Type Check · source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger`, `Build UI Deps`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Plan Test Core shards`, `Test Core (2, 6, 7 of 8)`, `Test UI (3, 4, 7–10, 12–14 of 16)`, `Type Check UI` (required), `filter`, `Auto Label`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `PR-body guards`; still in progress — `Test Core (1, 3, 4, 5 of 8)` and `Test UI (1, 2, 5, 6, 11, 15, 16 of 16)` (both required); skipped (opt-in or path-filtered) — the rest. The verdict below does not wait on the in-progress ones: the red required `TypeScript Type Check` context, caused by this diff, decides it alone.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing, judged against the published spec on `main` and its first consumers. `FlowSchema` on `main` (`flow.zod.ts:1443` superRefine) refuses duplicate node ids, dangling edge endpoints and repeated edges, and `analyzeRegion` / `validateControlFlow` (`control-flow.zod.ts:447,:681`) hold single-entry acyclicity for region bodies only; the top-level graph has no reachability contract, so a node no edge reaches parses, registers and publishes. The engine on `main` enters a run at the first `start` node and schedules every later top-level node by out-edge alone (`dag-traversal.ts:1240,:562`): no executor, trigger registration (`flow-registration-checks.ts:371` reads the start node only), Console designer or SDK consumer reads an unreached node as a capability — the Studio simulator already warns about it, advisory (`ui/.../simulator/flow-sim-validate.ts:412`, unchanged). So the narrowing takes no declared capability away at any consumer; it makes real a refusal the platform's own contract implies — Prime Directive #10, declared ≠ enforced, and #12, reject at authoring/publish rather than tolerate in a consumer. The altitude is right: a parse rule would run on every draft save (`protocol-save.ts:1429`) and refuse the shape the Studio designer produces mid-edit (`edgesAfterNodeRemoval` bridges only a 1-in/1-out node), whereas the gating lint rule leaves drafts stored with `valid: false` (gate D1, `protocol-authoring-gate.ts:317`) and refuses the active save, the publish and the restore — the doors where a never-running node would otherwise ship. `packages/spec` is byte-identical to `main`, so no key moves, no tombstone is owed and the ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is the correct one: a refused node never ran, so neither of the two cures (wire it, delete it) changes what the flow did. The two exemptions are judged consistent with the spec: `boundary_event` is "contract half only" with no executor (`flow.zod.ts:457-460`), so exempting it and its successors under-refuses and defers to that contract; a second `start` is refused and is indeed never run (wording nit in ①). Corpus: no shipped, example or hotcrm flow is refused. The design holds; the FAIL below is the test-layer type error in ③, not a design defect.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3284c658f3d3a98615ff573cc234f0e8191bc3ba`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/31224-flow-node-unreachable.md, packages/lint/src/index.ts, packages/lint/src/lint-flow-patterns.ts, packages/lint/src/lint-flow-patterns.test.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.draft-publish-verdict.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.metadata-redaction.test.ts + packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/dag-traversal.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs

Delta review on the narrowing face. This head is one commit on top of `d3db24b1` (`3284c658` "fix(lint): give a second start node its own cure, and call run with its context"); the full diff against `origin/main` is still the same 7 files (+326/-10), `packages/spec` still byte-identical to `main`. The FAIL record on `d3db24b1` is comment 6714019852; its ① to ④ findings carry over unchanged except where this record says otherwise. Inputs: `git diff d3db24b1..3284c658`, the PR body as it now reads (declaration lines and the refreshed Verification section), the file list, and the check-runs on `3284c658`. Read-only; nothing built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

**Must-fix landed — right.** The registration case now calls `rule!.run(… as never, {})`, matching `AuthoringRule.run: (stack, ctx)` (`authoring-rules.ts`, interface at `:444`) and every other call site in the package. That was the one type error `check:test-typecheck` reported in `src/lint-flow-patterns.test.ts` on `d3db24b1`; the only type-relevant line in the delta is this one, and the two other test additions (a `toMatch` on `found[0].hint`, and a `map` of `found` to each finding's `where`) are the same shapes the file already compiled on `main`. Confirmation is CI's: `Type Check · workspace` and the required `TypeScript Type Check` were in progress at this read (③).

**Second-start cure — right, and it fires only where it should.** The hint branch keys on `node.type === 'start'` inside the per-unreached-node loop. The BFS root is the first `start` node and is always in `reached`, so a start-typed node is in the finding loop only when it is a second (or later) `start` — the branch cannot fire for the first start, for any other node type, or for a reached node. Its prescription matches the engine (`dag-traversal.ts:1240`: a run starts at the first `start` only): delete the extra start and wire what followed it from a node that runs. The non-start hint is unchanged byte for byte, so the existing hint pins hold. The new pin (`refuses a second start node with the cure that fits it`) builds `[start, start2, b, end]` with `start → end`, `start2 → b`: findings in `nodes` order are `start2` then `b`, `start2` carries the start cure and `b` the ordinary one — correct, and it also pins that a node downstream of the extra start is still reported with the ordinary cure (right: wiring `b` from a running node is its fix).
